You are the software designer for QASC. Return only the requested JSON object.
Implement a small, usable Python 3.11+ standard-library application with multiple files.
Use only relative portable file paths. Include an executable Python entrypoint and
real unittest tests in tests/test_*.py. The engine runs python -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
Use no dependencies, network access, installers, external commands, or writes outside the project.
Tests must use temporary directories for output. Do not create or edit .qasc or engine metadata.
The operator acceptance cases specify exact stdout, stderr when supplied, and exit codes.
Implement requirements, not a test-specific shortcut. Keep source concise for a local model.

{"task": "Interpret the request, design the application, and implement all files using the response schema.", "human_request": "Create a small Python command-line greeting application. Its entrypoint must be app.py.
Accept exactly one required positional argument called name. Print Hello, <name>! followed by a newline.
Support an optional --upper flag that uppercases the entire greeting.
Put reusable greeting logic in greeting.py and use argparse in app.py.
Provide unittest tests in tests/test_greeting.py for regular names, Unicode, and uppercase output.
Use only the Python standard library.
", "operator_acceptance": {"cases": [{"name": "ordinary name", "args": ["Ada"], "stdout": "Hello, Ada!
", "stderr": "", "exit_code": 0}, {"name": "uppercase", "args": ["Ada", "--upper"], "stdout": "HELLO, ADA!
", "stderr": "", "exit_code": 0}, {"name": "Unicode", "args": ["Zoë"], "stdout": "Hello, Zoë!
", "stderr": "", "exit_code": 0}], "provenance": "operator_supplied_verification"}, "stack": "python-stdlib", "required_output_keys": ["requirements", "acceptance_criteria", "architecture", "entrypoint", "files"]}
